two-top/acb75c1:
THE SIZE-UP. Duelists 16->20, fangs 10->13, pickups 16->20 (half-extents,
cm), with every sprite following its own hitbox: the player sprite 80->100
and the foot offset with it, the fang already derived from
BOOMERANG_HALF_EXTENT_CM, and the pickup — which was a hardcoded 24 in app
quietly overwriting render's derived 1.8x every frame — now derived once in
render::pickup_render_size() and shared. Two other paths were available and
both were worse: inflating sprites alone breaks the what-you-see-is-what-
kills law the render layer is built on, and zooming the camera costs the
fairness invariant that every device sees the whole arena. The stage and
its cover are untouched, so the same board now holds a bigger cast; every
hit distance in the game moves with it, which is the point.

duelist before its own recall press, making that press a legitimate fresh
arm. Both are now written against v12's numbers.

perennials/ac0cf95:
Permapeople serves two images per plant -- `thumb` at 300px on the long edge and
`title` at 800px -- and the transform only ever read `thumb`. That is the real
reason the plant page looked soft: a 300px photo was being stretched across the
width of the screen, and no amount of resizing or compression fixes an upscale.
I said as much earlier and was wrong; the pixels were there the whole time.

The pipeline now carries both. The resizer works from the 800px one, which makes
every output sharper -- downscaling 800 -> 192 keeps detail that downscaling
300 -> 192 cannot -- so the card thumbnails improve too, not just the big photo.
The width ladder reaches 800 because that is where the source stops.

Retuned for the new source. The unsharp pass was calibrated for a 1.5x downscale
from 300px; from 800px a card thumb is a 4x downscale, so the old sigma was
manufacturing high-frequency detail a 56-pixel box cannot show and charging her
the bytes for it. Measured at 192px: 27.8 KB before, 14.2 KB now, and sharper.

Also fixed a bug the change exposed: the resizer's in-memory cache is keyed on
plant and width alone, so after a source refresh changed which origin a plant
resizes from, it went on serving renders made from the old, smaller image
forever. It is cleared when the source is replaced.

/health now reports photo coverage: 4,736 of 8,800 plants have a photograph.
The other 4,064 have none in Permapeople -- it serves a shared blank.jpg for
those, which the transform detects and nulls, so the guide says "no photo"
rather than showing a placeholder and calling it a plant.
